new_statements.quote: Stress is not attested to be lexically contrastive Patani, as no minimal pairs distinguished by stress are found. Based on a preliminary auditory analysis of non-monosyllabic words spoken in isolation, which were translated from Burung’s 2011 word list in Malay, Patani appears to have ultimate word stress as the main pattern: 49/62 polysyllabic words (the majority of which were disyllabic) were perceived as having a more prominent ultimate syllable. The remaining 13 words are all perceived as having penultimate stress. [...] To summarise, Patani appears to have ultimate stress as the main pattern.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not contrastive. In words spoken in isolation, prominence falls on the final (ultimate) syllable as the main pattern (49 of 62 polysyllabic words, mostly disyllables); the remaining 13 were heard as penultimate. Based on auditory impression only; the author explicitly says it needs instrumental confirmation and that the system may turn out to be phrasal accent rather than word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: 13/62 words perceived as penultimate; the same word may be realised differently by different speakers (tɛlɛ 'banana': penultimate prominence for speaker BM2, ultimate for MM1, Figs 2.1–2.2), with the final syllable longest in both (possible phrase-final lengthening); consultants gave no clear response when asked to choose between penultimate and ultimate realisations. Fn. 22: this makes Patani stand out, since most described SHWNG languages are reported to have fixed antepenultimate stress (Gasser et al. 2024) and Kamholz (2014: 13) reconstructs Proto-SHWNG penultimate stress. §2.4.4.1 (pp. 52–53): base and applicative verb forms both have ultimate stress; syncope deletes the vowel preceding the stressed syllable.
new_statements.domain_note: Polysyllabic words spoken in isolation (citation forms elicited via a Malay wordlist). The author raises the possibility that the domain is the phrase rather than the word ("the observed acoustic prominence is in fact phrasal accent rather than word stress", citing Goedemans & van Zanten 2014: 91–92). §2.5.2 separately describes expressive lengthening of the final vowel of the phonological word with a pitch rise (intensifying meaning). Impressionistic, not instrumental.
new_statements.identity_note: Rødvand 2024 describes the southern (Banemo, kecamatan Patani Barat) variety of Patani (§1.1.2, §1.4.1.1: 'the description in this dissertation is mainly based on the southern, Banemo variety'); a northern variety (Tepeleo) differs lexically and, per speakers, in intonation. Glottolog pata1260 has no dialect-level languoids, so the statement maps to pata1260 with a Banemo/southern-dialect caveat.

Also §2.4.4.1 (pp. 52–53): base and applicative verb forms both have ultimate stress.
